Exemption granted, subject to just exceptions.
Let requisite compliances be made within 01 week.
The application stands disposed of.

2.

The genesis of the matter are title verification/legal search reports ('search reports') rendered by the petitioner, who is a lady lawyer about 71 years of age, on the panel of the Punjab National Bank.

sentences.text: The petitioner was tasked to verify certain title documents relating to a property that was proposed to be placed by a guarantor as security/collateral towards a loan to be extended by the bank, and the search reports were drawn-up and submitted for that purpose.
3. Chargesheet dated 22.12.2017 has been filed in the matter.
The petitioner is arrayed as accused No. 6 in the proceedings before the learned Trial Court.

4. Mr. Madhav Khurana, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has drawn attention of this court to the following portions of the impugned order, which are relevant for the purpose of the present proceedings :
"7.

It was further revealed in the investigation that the Panel Lawyer of PNB, Smt.
Sudha Verma (A-6) in her Legal Search Report dated 03.08.2012 and 04.08.2012,
falsely

stated that she conducted investigation of the title with regard to the aforesaid two immovable properties kept as collaterals falsely mentioning the particulars with regard to registration number, date and page etc. shown in the respective Sale Deeds of the aforesaid properties.

The contents of the Sale Deeds were also shown matching with the information as sought in the records of Sub-Registrar and the photographs of the previous owner and of intending mortgagor affixed in the title deed, also shown tallying with the records of the registration kept in the Sub-Registrar Office.

It was further revealed that cash receipt of Rs. 1,000/- vide Slip No. 1253 dated 03.08.2012 shown to have been issued to accused Sudha Verma, Advocate for This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 17/07/2024 at 02:19:45 inspection of record for 2003-12 by the Office of Sub-Registrar-II, Janakpuri, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as 'Sub-Registrar')
but as per the office record of Sub-Registrar, the said receipt was generated on 17.11.2011 and that too in the name of V. Shankra for Rs. 30/- in respect of providing certified copies of some other documents.

"60. Now coming to the allegations and material against accused Sudha Verma,
Panel Lawyer of PNB, Investigation Agency/CBI has placed on record ample material to show that she prepared a false Legal Search Report dated 03.08.2012 and 04.08.2012 in respect of the mortgaged Properties without visiting and verifying the title documents in respect thereto.

In addition to the aforesaid, she prepared forged and fabricated receipts/slips falsely showing inspection of the title documents in respect of aforesaid Properties with offices of Sub-Registrar concerned.
The details of the said receipts/slips have already been mentioned above under the heading 'Brief Facts'.

"63. In view of the aforesaid settled law applying to the facts and circumstances of the present case, in respect of role played by accused Sudha Verma being Panel Sudha Verma vs Central Bureau Of Investigation on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161600667/

sentences.text: Advocate, this Court finds that there is sufficient material available on record, prima facie, showing her involvement in the commission of offences U/s 420 & 471 IPC and U/s 120B read with Section 13 (2) read with Section 13(1)(d) of PC Act, as she not only failed to verify the title deeds as per Bank Circulars but also filed forged and fabricated receipts/slips falsely showing that she inspected the title documents with office of Sub Registrar."

(emphasis supplied)
5. Mr. Khurana argues, that even though the search reports tendered by the petitioner may have been the result of professional negligence on her part as a lawyer, in that she may not have conducted proper verification of the title documents herself, no case is made-out for framing charges against the petitioner under sections 420/471/120-B This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 17/07/2024 at 02:19:46 IPC and section 13(2) read with section 13(1)(d) PC Act, since there is no allegation that the petitioner induced anyone to deliver any property or valuable security; nor is there any allegation that she received any illegal gratification; nor that she colluded with the borrower in any manner in connection with the disbursal of loan by the bank.
6.

Mr. Khurana submits, that to be sure, there is no allegation in the charge-sheet that any dishonest inducement by the petitioner led to the bank paying her professional fee, which was the only financial transactions between the petitioner and the bank; and there was no financial transaction whatsoever between the petitioner and any of the other persons concerned with the disbursal of the loan.

7. Mr. Khurana has placed reliance upon a decision of the Supreme Court in Central Bureau of Investigation, Hyderabad vs. K. Narayana Rao,1 to submit that a perusal of paras 3, 20, 21, 28, 30 &
31 of that judgment would show that that case involved an almost exact same fact situation as the one obtaining in the present matter.
8.

entities.text: Central Bureau of Investigation, Hyderabad vs. K. Narayana Rao,1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Khurana submits that in K. Narayana Rao (supra), the Supreme Court had held as follows :
"30. Therefore, the liability against an opining advocate arises only when the lawyer was an active participant in a plan to defraud the Bank.
In the given case, there is no evidence to prove that A-6 was abetting or aiding the original conspirators.

"31. However, it is beyond doubt that a lawyer owes an "unremitting loyalty" to the interests of the client and it is the lawyer's responsibility to act in a manner that would best advance the interest of the client.
Merely because his opinion may not be acceptable, he cannot be mulcted with the criminal prosecution, (2012) 9 SCC 512 This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 17/07/2024 at 02:19:47 particularly, in the absence of tangible evidence that he associated with other conspirators.

At the most, he may be liable for gross negligence or professional misconduct if it is established by acceptable evidence and cannot be charged for the offence under Sections 420 and 109 IPC along with other conspirators without proper and acceptable link between them.

It is further made clear that if there is a link or evidence to connect him with the other conspirators for causing loss to the institution, undoubtedly, the prosecuting authorities are entitled to proceed under criminal prosecution.
Such tangible materials are lacking in the case of the respondent herein."
(emphasis supplied)

9. It is accordingly argued that, in the present case, the critical element of dishonestly inducing the bank to disburse the loan to the borrower, is missing against the petitioner, especially since the bank's decision to grant the loan could not have proceeded solely on the basis of the search reports furnished by the petitioner.

It is also pointed-out that in the search reports furnished, the petitioner had categorically stated in several places that certified copies of the sale deeds, which were to be submitted by the guarantor towards the loan, had been applied-for; and that, in any case, the guarantor had to place the originals of those title documents with the bank before disbursal of the loan.

Mr. Khurana argues, that this shows, firstly, that the petitioner had caveated her search reports with certain requirements that were to be completed before disbursal of the loan, which the bank ought to have followed; and secondly, the fact that the petitioner had put such caveats in her search reports show that she was not in any way involved with the borrower or the guarantor; and accordingly the element of criminality is prima-facie ruled-out.

On a prima-facie view of the matter, issue notice.
11. Mr. Atul Guleria, learned SPP appears on behalf of the respondent/CBI on advance copy; accepts notice; and seeks time to file counter- affidavit.

12. Let counter-affidavit be filed within 06 weeks; rejoinder thereto, if any, be filed within 04 weeks;
with copies to the opposing counsel.

13. Learned SPP submits, that being the panel lawyer who was tasked to tender a title-verification report to the bank, the petitioner owed a duty to do proper verification before furnishing the search reports.

He draws attention of this court to an allegedly forged Cash Receipt, which purports to show that the petitioner had visited the Sub-Registrar's office for inspection of documents, which was however, not true.

15. On a prima-facie view of the matter, in the opinion of this court, the petitioner was involved in the loan transaction to the limited extent of having tendered search reports, and there is no allegation in the chargesheet nor any observation in the impugned order, that the petitioner had any greater role than that in the loan transaction.
Moreover, there is no allegation that the petitioner has received any illegal gratification or favour, in lieu of which she tendered the search reports.
